name: DWG FastView
tagline: Browser, mobile, and desktop clients to open, annotate, and share DWG without a full CAD seat.
meta_desc: Anchored at en.dwgfastview.com—useful for field markup, investor reviews, and quick measurement. Editing depth is intentionally narrower than desktop GstarCAD; check SDK/licensing separately if you embed viewers in your own apps.

terms.title: Mobile CAD Annotation
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Mobile CAD Annotation inside DWG FastView.
terms.definition: Mobile CAD Annotation places drawing comments and dimensions on drawings using mobile screens.
terms.why_matters: Improves contractor communication by allowing inspectors to log issues directly on drawings.
common_pitfalls: Drawing sketches without locking dimensions, causing annotation shifts
Annotating old local file revisions instead of the active cloud master

quiz.question: When working with Mobile CAD Annotation, which of the following represents a common technical pitfall?
options: Drawing sketches without locking dimensions, causing annotation shifts.
Failing to manually re-index the SQL server database.
Over-allocating virtual memory caches in the cloud settings.
Restricting linetype scales strictly to 1:1 paper coordinates.
quiz.explanation: Correct. A common pitfall is 'Drawing sketches without locking dimensions, causing annotation shifts.' As the editorial review notes: 'Improves contractor communication by allowing inspectors to log issues directly on drawings.'

terms.title: Cross-Platform Drawing Share
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Cross-Platform Drawing Share inside DWG FastView.
terms.definition: Cross-Platform Drawing Share syncs markups and annotations between mobile, browser, and desktop users.
terms.why_matters: Eliminates markup transcribing errors and links office teams to site workers.
common_pitfalls: Sharing drawing files without merging active markup layers first
Neglecting font catalog differences causing text reflow errors

quiz.question: When working with Cross-Platform Drawing Share, which of the following represents a common technical pitfall?
options: Sharing drawing files without merging active markup layers first.
Failing to manually re-index the SQL server database.
Over-allocating virtual memory caches in the cloud settings.
Restricting linetype scales strictly to 1:1 paper coordinates.
quiz.explanation: Correct. A common pitfall is 'Sharing drawing files without merging active markup layers first.' As the editorial review notes: 'Eliminates markup transcribing errors and links office teams to site workers.'

terms.title: Offline Drawing Storage
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Offline Drawing Storage inside DWG FastView.
terms.definition: Offline Drawing Storage caches drawing files in local device memory for access without network.
terms.why_matters: Enables site reviews in remote areas or basement structures with weak signals.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to load files while online before traveling to offline sites
Making offline edits that conflict with updates made by other team members

faqs.question: How to use markup tools on mobile devices?
faqs.answer: Open a drawing, select Edit mode, choose the markup toolbar, and use your finger or stylus to draw clouds, text annotations, or linear dimensions.

faqs.question: Can I view CAD drawing files when my device is offline?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the drawing file while online to cache it in local memory, or manually download it to the Offline tab for disconnected work.

faqs.question: How to sync annotations with the office team?
faqs.answer: Save the annotated drawing back to the cloud space. Other team members will receive notifications and see markups instantly.
